Mr. President of the UNDP Executive Board, distinguished members of this Executive Board, esteemed Permanent Representative of the Federal Republic— Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, and of course representatives of all our member states who are present, colleagues, ladies and gentlemen, Good afternoon. Really pleased today to present for your approval to this annual session of the Joint UNDP/UNFPA/UNOPS Executive Board the Country Program Document for the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. Mr. President, distinguished members, Ethiopia is at a pivotal moment. It is emerging from the combined effects and shocks of the COVID-19 pandemic and the conflicts that it has experienced in the northern part of the country, while at the same time undergoing very bold economic reforms. The country's macroeconomic outlook is actually quite positive. Real GDP growth reached 8.1% in 2024, and is projected to remain strong. This is driven by robust performance in the industrial, services, and agriculture sectors. Inflation is on a downward trend, supported by sound macroeconomic management and prudent policy actions, including the flotation of the currency in July 2024. These measures have helped to narrow the exchange rate gap and also catalyzed significant international support, notably securing an extended credit facility from the IMF and additional financial support from the World Bank. But despite this progress, Ethiopia continues to face pressing humanitarian and development challenges. The government has prioritized protection of the most vulnerable through expanded safety net programs, continued fertilizer subsidies, and civil servants' salary adjustments. While it is doing this, it is also phasing out utility subsidies and advancing fiscal and debt management reforms that are focused on safeguarding social spending and improving revenue mobilization. In this context, the 2025-2030 Country Programme Document, anchored on the principle of leaving no one behind, is designed to be responsive as much as possible and also forward-looking, supporting the governments efforts through 3 strategic pillars. The first is strengthening democratic governance and peacebuilding. Second pillar is advancing inclusive economic transformation with a focus specifically on micro, small, and medium enterprises. Focus on youth. and a focus on women. The third is promoting climate resilience and environmental sustainability. Mr. President, distinguished Executive Board members, as is really our standard practice, the country program document was developed through extensive consultations with the government of Ethiopia, in the first instance, and also a broad array of stakeholders, including, of course, our sister UN agencies, the UN system overall, bilateral, multilateral partners, civil society partners, and, of course, the private sector. The draft program document before you is tailored to the national development priorities It is fully aligned with Ethiopia's 10-year development plan, the homegrown economic reform agenda, the NDCs, the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework, but also the agendas of the UN and the African Union. It also reflects the core elements of the UNDP strategic plan, which is currently being finalized, 2026. To 2029, ensuring continued strategic coherence and relevance. Mr. President, distinguished members of the Executive Board, at a time when development needs in Africa are both urgent and expansive, the Ethiopia Country Program document presents a timely and strategic opportunity for deepened partner engagement. Evidence continues to demonstrate that that development cooperation is not only a moral imperative, but it is also a smart economic strategy. For instance, a recent policy brief by ODIHR, which is titled Modeling the Impact of EU Aid on EU Economies, shows that every €1 invested in EU aid yields a total return of €1.50. While this study focuses on the EU, the broader message is actually clear: investing in development, especially in dynamic and high-potential contexts such as Ethiopia, generates shared benefits, bolsters global prosperity, and reinforces long-term economic interdependence. These findings underscore the value of sustaining and scaling up development cooperation, particularly in the Africa region, where the dividends of shared prosperity and mutual benefit are increasingly evident. As we say in UNDP Africa, the Africa we want is really the Africa the world needs. We hope that the Ethiopia Country Program Document will garner the continued and reinforced support of development partners, given its strong potential to generate national, regional, and global gains. Mr. President, we respectfully request the Executive Board's approval of the CPD for the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia and the 4th year CPD extension for Burkina Faso. We also note, for the Board's information, the Administrator's approval of the first CPD extensions for South Africa and South Sudan. I really would like here to reiterate my appreciation to the government of Ethiopia for the continued collaboration and to reaffirm UNDP's commitment to supporting the government and the people of Ethiopia in delivering on this program and to working closely with all partners to achieve its objectives. Allow me to conclude, Mr. President, by expressing our sincere appreciation to you, Mr. President, and to all members of the Executive Board for your continued support to the UNDP Regional Bureau for Africa and to all program countries under its coverage. I thank you for your attention.
Thank you.

Thank you, Mr. President, for giving me the floor. Distinguished members of the Executive Board, Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, it's a great honor for me to address the Executive Board in my national capacity as a representative of the Government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia on the Country Programme Document, CPD, for the period July 2025 to June 2030. At the outset, I wish to express our sincere appreciation to the United Nations Development Programme for its partnership, and to the Executive Board for its steadfast support to countries like Ethiopia in our efforts to achieve inclusive and sustainable development. The CPD is the outcome of a broad and inclusive consultation process involving government institutions, civil society, the private sector, and development partners. It's fully aligned with Ethiopia's 10-Year Development Plan, the Sustainable Development Goals, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework 2025-2030. The document outlines a 5-year strategic framework built around 3 key pillars that reflect our national priorities, as indicated by the ESG earlier. The first one, democratic governance and sustaining peace. This pillar focuses on strengthening institutional capacity, advancing national dialogue and transitional justice, and deepening civil service and electoral reforms. It promotes inclusive governance by ensuring the active participation of women and youth in peacebuilding and leadership processes. The second pillar, inclusive economic transformation. This pillar seeks to foster equitable and sustainable economic growth through private sector development, expanded access to finance for MSMEs and startups, and the creation of decent jobs. Emphasis is placed on digital innovation, particularly for youth and women, as a driver of inclusive growth. Our 3rd pillar is resilience and environmental sustainability. This component aims to enhance Ethiopia's ability to respond to the climate and environmental challenges through stronger disaster risk management, increased access to affordable renewable energy, and promotion of climate-smart agricultural practices. Mobilizing climate finance is also central to achieving a green, resilient economy. Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, these strategic priorities are designed to address Ethiopia's development challenges, ranging from poverty to environmental vulnerability, to building peace through an integrated and forward-looking approach. To realize these priorities, a total of $279.3 million is required over the next 5 years. This CPD is not only a strategic document; it represents a shared commitment to results grounded in national ownership, and informed by the lessons of the 2024 Independent Country Programme Evaluation. We respectfully request the Executive Board's endorsement and call on all partners to support its successful implementation. The Government of Ethiopia reaffirms its full commitment to the partnership and its effective delivery. I thank you, Mr. President.

Muchísimas gracias, señor presidente. Muy buenas tardes. Excellencies, distinguished delegates, it's an honor to address you today and introduce Item 17, UNFPA Country Programs and Related Matters. Today we present the new Ethiopia Country Program document for 2025-2030 from the East and Southern Africa region. The total budget is $140.4 million, with 17% allocated from regular resources. The program was developed through close collaboration with the Government of Ethiopia, the UN Country Team, and diverse national and regional stakeholders. It fully upholds the principle of national ownership. This marks UNFPA's 10th program cycle in Ethiopia. It aligns strongly with Ethiopia's national development priorities and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework. The program reflects UNFPA's unwavering commitment to advancing the ICPD Programme of Action, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and the UNFPA Strategic Plan. It also builds on lessons learned from previous evaluations and has undergone rigorous internal quality assurance. Across Africa, progress is evident. Since 2000, maternal mortality has decreased by 40% in sub-Saharan Africa, In 2024 alone, UNFPA contributed to the prevention of 6.2 million unintended pregnancies and helped 6.5 million adolescents to access youth-friendly services in Eastern and Southern Africa. Yet, this progress remains fragile. Conflict, climate disruption, growing inequalities, and limited fiscal space continue to threaten hard-earned gains. We face growing resistance to sexual and reproductive health, stagnation in family planning uptake, and rising gender-based violence, especially in humanitarian contexts. Against this background, the Ethiopia Country Program aims to protect progress and scale what works. Let me highlight 4 key areas. First, we aim to double our impact in family planning. From 9 million couple-years of protection achieved in the last cycle, we now target 19 million. By 2030. Second, we will continue to support Ethiopia in reducing maternal mortality, which dropped 70% between 2000 and 2020. By strengthening health systems, midwifery, and maternal services, we aim to halve maternal mortality again during this cycle. Third, we will scale up efforts to eliminate gender-based violence and harmful practices. In the last cycle, over 1,000 communities pledged to end child marriage and female genital mutilation. We will work with government and local partners to reach even more communities going forward. Finally, we will invest in Ethiopia's youth. More than 1.3 million adolescents received life skills education in the last cycle. The new program aims to reach 2.5 million in line with National Adolescent Health and HIV Prevention Strategy. The Ethiopia CPD presented today is also guided by a strategic foresight analysis, identifying political governance and domestic financing as critical drivers for future success. The program emphasizes not only proven intervention, but also adaptability, collective action, and shift from traditional to more diversified financing model. Our goal is to ensure sustainability in a rapidly evolving environment. In a few moments, the Regional Director will offer further insight to the program. Distinguished delegates, in addition to Ethiopia Country Program presented for approval, the Board may wish to note that the Executive Director has approved a 6-month extension of the South Africa Country Program in line with established procedure. We thank you for your feedback during the formal commenting period and for your ongoing support for UNFPA work. Together, we can ensure that women and girls everywhere live healthy, dignified, and empowered lives. I thank you for your kind attention.

Chair, distinguished members of the Executive Board, Ethiopia, a cornerstone of the Horn of Africa, Africa stands as a testament to the enduring spirit and transformative potential of a nation committed to inclusive development. With its rich history, cultural diversity, and youthful population, Ethiopia is forging a path of resilience, innovation, and hope, creating opportunities where challenges once prevailed. One remarkable example comes from the town of Hewane, Tigray, where a group of mothers have shown extraordinary resilience. These women, whose lives were disrupted by conflict, have turned adversity into opportunity. With UNFPA's support, they received psychological counseling, skills training in sheep husbandry, and financial literacy. What began as a path to recovery has evolved into a thriving cooperative embodying unity, empowerment, and resilience. The journey of these women reflects the resilience and determination that define Ethiopia and the broader Eastern Southern Africa region. Their story shows how community-driven solutions and women-led empowerment are shaping a more equitable and sustainable future for all. It is with this spirit of resilience and ambition that I present the draft Country Programme for Ethiopia for the period 2025 to 2030. A forward-looking program designed to accelerate progress in the final stretch towards the 2030 Agenda. The program builds on Ethiopia's commitment to the UNFPA transformative results and supports national efforts to advance gender equality, improve maternal and reproductive health, and harness the potential of its young people as the country works towards its long-term vision for inclusive and sustainable development. As UNFPA, we are proud to note that in the last 2 decades, Ethiopia's maternal mortality ratio declined from 871 per 100,000 live births in 2000 to 267 per 100,000 live births in 2020. The modern contraceptive prevalence rate among married women increased from 14% in 2005 to 41% in 2019.

Shifts in the financing landscape and humanitarian crisis exacerbate these issues, further restricting access to essential services. Distinguished members of the Board, with a $140 million funding envelope, the UNFPA Country Programme for Ethiopia will support the Government of Ethiopia in achieving measurable impacts to address these challenges. Through strategic shifts aimed at enhancing quality of services, building resilience, empowering women and youth, and leveraging innovation and partnerships, UNFPA seeks to drive transformative change.
